title: §498 BGB — termination of a consumer loan on default
summary: A dependency-led research map for §498 BGB rather than a paraphrase of the provision. The research graph expands only where claims genuinely depend on other material: classification and scope, form requirements, default consequences, cost consequences after acceleration, the mandatory-law boundary, case law, legislative history, and EU consumer-credit law.
evidence: dependency nodes: §491, §492, §497, §501, §512 BGB, plus BGH and OLG interpretation of the qualified notice
the example ledger carries three claims and all three are UNESTABLISHED with NOT_RETRIEVED evidence
the derived claim C-498-REPORT-PLAN names both premises and its derivation rule
the example asserts a research plan, explicitly not a current or complete legal analysis
friction: The first instinct for 'a complete report on §498' was to gather sources broadly. The dependency-led approach forces the opposite: expand only where a claim genuinely depends on other material, which makes the map smaller and the gaps visible.

All three example claims came out UNESTABLISHED, which looked like a failed example until it became the point. A research plan is not a legal conclusion, and the example had to stop pretending otherwise.
notes: The lender's right to terminate on default is an option written into the contract. Pairs directly with hazard-rate modelling.
